title: August and the Terminal
premise: Freya Sterling smuggles forbidden memory-records through orbital customs above Meridian, a dying colony whose terraforming failed decades ago and whose fate the interstellar powers have agreed to erase from official record. When the colony's children begin sharing a single recursive dream — a dream Freya discovers is a broadcast from a buried archive her late mother helped build — she realizes the colony's founders encoded a truth that could reignite war between the two fleets blockading Meridian's orbit. To keep the fragile peace, Freya must fabricate a false version of the archive's message and smuggle it into both fleets' command streams, while the real memory, and the children who carry it, slowly burn through her. In the end she chooses to release the true memory anyway, sacrificing her ship and her smuggler's identity, and the colony's children — her found family — carry the truth outward as the fleets, forced to confront what they buried, withdraw together.
about_author: August Thackeray is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years on station before trading manifests for manuscripts. They write science fiction about people who keep records the universe would prefer lost.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Heart
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She runs a memory-chip past Meridian customs inside a coffin of frozen seed stock, establishing her trade, her cynicism, and the colony's slow suffocation below. Emotional beat: weary competence masking grief she won't name.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A customs officer named Idris Voss flags her shipment — not to arrest her, but to warn her that both blockading fleets have begun auditing Meridian's data traffic. Beat: first crack in her sense of control.

chapters.title: Children of the Static
chapters.summary: Colony teacher Amara Osei's POV. Her students fall asleep mid-lesson and wake reciting identical coordinates. She records the phenomenon on a chip she shouldn't have. Beat: wonder edged with dread.

chapters.title: What My Mother Buried
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Sorting her late mother's effects, Freya finds survey notes matching the children's coordinates — her mother helped build the buried Meridian Archive. Beat: inheritance as burden, not gift.

chapters.title: Downwell
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She descends to Meridian against her own rules, meets Amara and the dreaming children, and touches the archive's surface — the dream flickers into her mind. Beat: the smuggler becomes cargo.

chapters.title: The Dream's First Verse
chapters.summary: Shared-dream sequence, Freya and the children. The archive shows Meridian's founding and a deliberate act of sabotage — one fleet's, officially blamed on the other. Beat: revelation that rewrites history.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Idris Voss's POV. He pieces together why the Concord and the Halcyon Compact both blockade Meridian: the peace between them rests on the colony staying forgotten. Beat: the machinery of silence revealed.

chapters.title: Amara's Choice
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Fleet agents arrive asking about her students. She hides the children's dream-journal and lies for the first time in her careful life. Beat: a protector forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Weight of the Chip
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She realizes the true memory, leaked, means war; suppressed, it means the children keep dreaming until it breaks them. She drafts a forged archive message. Beat: the lie takes shape, and she hates how good she is at it.

chapters.title: Nine Sleepers
chapters.summary: The eldest dreamer, twelve-year-old Juno, POV. The dream is changing her — she remembers things that never happened to her, including her grandmother's face at the sabotage. Beat: identity dissolving into inherited memory.

chapters.title: Customs and Consequences
chapters.summary: Freya and Idris, alternating. She recruits him to plant the forged memory in both fleets' command streams; he risks his career and his certainty. Beat: reluctant alliance becoming trust.

chapters.title: The Forgery
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She edits her mother's own voice into a benign version of the archive — a betrayal and a tribute at once. Beat: grief weaponized.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The planting operation half-succeeds: the Concord accepts the forgery, but the Halcyon Compact traces its origin to Meridian and dispatches an interrogation team. Beat: victory curdling into countdown.

chapters.title: What the Children Keep
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. The Compact team takes blood samples from the dreamers. Amara realizes the children themselves are now evidence — and targets. Beat: maternal terror.

chapters.title: Juno Remembers the Fleet
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Deep in the dream, Juno finds the sabotage's author — a Compact officer whose descendants now command the blockade. Beat: the past reaching up through a child.

chapters.title: The Lie Begins to Die
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The forged memory destabilizes; the children's real dream is bleeding through the falsified broadcast, and both fleets detect the contradiction. Beat: her masterpiece failing in real time.

chapters.title: Evacuation of the Innocent
chapters.summary: Amara and Idris, alternating. They move the nine children off-world under coffin-manifests, Freya's old trick turned to rescue. Beat: found family assembled under fire.

chapters.title: The Terminal
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, at the buried archive. Cornered by both fleets' agents, she must choose: complete the forgery and survive, or broadcast the true memory and end the peace. Beat: the novel's moral fulcrum.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She releases everything — the sabotage, the cover-up, her mother's voice — and burns the archive's uplink and her ship's transponder to do it. Beat: sacrifice as authorship.

chapters.title: Fleets in the Same Room
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Commanders of Concord and Compact, confronted with shared evidence, meet for the first time in thirty years — not as enemies but as co-authors of a lie. Beat: shame as the beginning of peace.

chapters.title: The Long Wake
chapters.summary: Amara and Juno's POV. The dream ends; the children grieve the memories that were never theirs and begin choosing which ones to keep. Beat: identity rebuilt from inheritance, not defined by it.

chapters.title: August and the Terminal
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue. Stripped of ship, license, and alias, she stays on Meridian as its first honest archivist while the children's testimony travels outward with the withdrawing fleets. Beat: the smuggler finally delivering something true.
